_about_scoringWeights: Three-component score blend per DF-2b. inference + methodAppropriateness + accuracy must sum to 1.0 (engine validates at load). Tune these per scenario to weight what each cohort should learn most.

default.name: Stationary Demand — Stevenson Ch. 3 baseline
default.description: Baseline operations-management drill. Roughly horizontal weekly demand (mean ~100) with random noise. Suited to Naive, Moving Average, and Exponential Smoothing. 20 periods total, 5 warmup periods of revealed history before forecasting begins.

trending-quarterly-retail.name: Trending Demand — Heizer Ch. 4 retail growth
trending-quarterly-retail.description: A growing-retail-chain scenario with a clean linear upward trend (slope +4 units/period) over a baseline of ~80. Naive and Moving Average will systematically under-forecast; Holt's Double Exponential Smoothing and Linear Regression should track best.

seasonal-quarterly.name: Seasonal Demand — quarterly cycle (audit D6 fix)
seasonal-quarterly.description: Quarterly seasonality (sinePeriod 4) over a stationary mean of 100. Audit D6 documented that the legacy engine had a 12-period sine mislabelled as quarterly; this scenario ships a true 4-period cycle so 20 periods give 5 clean cycles.

random-noise.name: Random Demand — pure white noise
random-noise.description: No trend, no seasonality, large noise around a baseline of 100. Naive forecasting is the canonical recommendation; sophisticated methods will overfit. Useful for showing students that complexity is not always better.
